problem:
The center of the hyperbola $9{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-54x=-56$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-54x & =-56 \\ 9{x}^{2}-54x\,-\,4{y}^{2} & =-56 \\ 9[{x}^{2}-6x]\,-\,4{y}^{2} & =-56 \\ 9[(x-3)^{2}-9]\,-\,4{y}^{2} & =-56 \\ 9(x-3)^{2}-81\,-\,4{y}^{2} & =-56 \\ 9(x-3)^{2}\,-\,4{y}^{2} & =25 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{{(\frac{5}{3})}^{2}}\,-\,\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(\frac{5}{2})}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,3,0\,).$
